newsitem.title: JORDAN: Amman stocks steady in moderate trade.
newsitem.headline: Amman stocks steady in moderate trade.

text.p: Jordan's bourse was steady on Sunday in moderate trade buttressed by speculative dealing in blue-chips which are widely anticipated to become targets of a possible resumed foreign buying spree, dealers said.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose a slight 0.05 percent to close at 159.69 points in turnover worth 751,503 dinars ($1.1 million).
"The market was stable today with an upward trend," said Mohammmed Adullah, senior analyst at Pearl Consulting.

Trading value has fallen sharply since last week after global funds pulled back from an aggressive two-week long buying spree, focused on mining blue-chip stocks and cement, which sent prices to their highest in nearly two years.
But investors are bracing for a revival in the coming few days in global fund activity on attractively priced blue-chips after a week-long pause on the back of some profit-taking, dealers said.
Bourse activity was underpinned by mostly local investor interest in a handful of industrial and bank blue-chips although some foreign orders were also detected for the same popular blue-chips.
"Local buying is in preparation of resumed foreign buying," said Ibrahim Odeh, broker at Wataniyeh Financial Services.
Main focus of interest was again on Jordan-National Bank which rose 2.97 percent to 2.08 dinars on deals worth 175,596 dinars.

The bank, with around 30 percent of its stock freely floated in the market, is one of the firms which funds have targeted among a handful of stocks viewed as potential candidates for a future GDR (Global Depository Receipt) listing.
Another stock which attracted some attention was leading drug manufacturer Dar al-Dawa, which rose by nearly the five percent daily limit to 5.48 dinars on deals worth 26,284 dinars.
But market favourite Jordan Cement, in the forefront of demand by foreign funds, shed 0.03 dinars to 4.07 dinars. It was the second most active share, with shares worth 112,460 dinars changing hands.
The third busiest traded firm was majority state owned Jordan Phosphate Mines which stood at 3.90 dinars in 66,219 dinars worth of trade.
Overall falling shares outnumbered gainers by 16 to 13 while another 18 traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance rose 0.36 percent to 81.15 points, 2.68 percent down from the start of the year.
